learning: If line_loss_events falls below 1 and max_error drops below 0.06 on the s-bend and slalom, turning authority was the limit and the next step is speed (wheel_radius). If max_error is unchanged, the limit is elsewhere, likely speed or sensor response. If oscillation rises above 0.15, the controller needs lower kp rather than more geometry change.
notes: Keeps the iteration 2 sensor array and iteration 2 controller unchanged. Only mass, body_length and wheel_track change, so the race isolates turning authority and yaw inertia. Steering oscillation is watched because the narrower track raises turn rate.
rationale: Iteration 2 showed that the sensor array is not the binding limit. Moving the span, footprint and lead changed max_error by under 0.001 m, and every track still ends off-track with one line-loss event and steering_oscillation of only 0.07 to 0.15. The robot drifts off the tape steadily rather than jittering, which points to limited turning authority at its current speed. This geometry keeps the iteration 2 sensor array exactly (x = -0.03 to 0.03 m at y = 0.04 m, 16 mm footprints) and changes the drivetrain and body: mass 0.6 to 0.5 kg, body_length 0.18 to 0.12 m, wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10 m. Narrowing the track raises turn rate per unit of wheel-speed difference, and the shorter, lighter body lowers yaw inertia. Because the change is geometric only, I keep the iteration 2 controller (base_speed 1.6, kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.1, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction) so any score change can be attributed to the geometry. Oscillation headroom exists (0.07 to 0.15 observed), so I do not lower kp pre-emptively. If the next race shows oscillation above 0.15 with the narrower track, the controller should reduce kp, not the geometry. I expect line_loss_events below 1 and max_error below 0.06 on the s-bend and slalom. Completion time is not yet testable because the robot has not held the line.
